handoff: Approve, no blocking findings. AC1, AC2 and AC9 are implemented with tests at the repo-rule and guard seams. Reran: unit 983 pass, typecheck clean, integration 505 pass, e2e 72 pass. Minor: unit tests can call allowSpawns() and switch the guard off; the by-name ban misses namespace imports of @norn/store.

findings.title: A unit test can switch the guard off with allowSpawns()
findings.detail:
Any unit test can import allowSpawns from test/support/unit-guard.ts, or import spawning-tier-preload.ts, and the guard then passes every spawn through. That is a side door that B4/B15's 'so that unit tests cannot reach real git by a side door' wants closed. It is not on D13's banned list, so it is not a criterion breach. test/repo/unit-guard.test.ts uses allowSpawns legitimately.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Add spawning-tier-preload.ts and named imports of allowSpawns (outside test/repo/unit-guard.test.ts) to the B15 rule.

findings.title: The by-name ban misses namespace and default-style imports of @norn/store
findings.detail:
STORE_NAMED only matches `import { … } from "@norn/store"`. `import * as store from "@norn/store"; store.fetchNornRefs(…)` passes the rule. The runtime guard would still catch the spawn, so the risk is low.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Also flag `import * as` from @norn/store in unit tests, or flag `.fetchNornRefs(` / `.onlyNornCommitsSince(` member uses.
